rounds.learn: Strings have methods. A method is a small action you run with a dot. .upper() turns every letter into a capital. .lower() makes them small.
rounds.task: Save a word in shout. Print it in capitals.
rounds.say: %out%. The dot reached into the string and ran upper() on it.

rounds.learn: A + between two strings glues them together. len() counts the characters in a string, spaces too.
rounds.task: Glue two words into one. Print it, then print how long it is.
rounds.code:
first = "tool"
second = "box"
word = first [[+]] second
print(word)
print([[len]](word))
rounds.say: toolbox, 7 letters. + glued them, len() counted.

rounds.task: Glue py and thon. Print the word in capitals. Then print its length.
rounds.say: PYTHON, then 6. Three moves, all from memory.

rounds.task: Make a variable called tool that holds hammer. Print it in capitals.
rounds.hint: tool = "hammer" on one line. Then print(tool.upper()).

checks.msg: Let .upper() do the capitals for you.

rounds.say: HAMMER. You called a method with nothing to copy.
